title_en: Notice of the General Office of the Supreme People's Court on Forwarding the Reply Opinion of the Legislative Affairs Commission of the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress on the Specific Application of Article 30 of the Customs Law
full_text_en:
General Office of the Supreme People's Court

Notice on Forwarding the "Reply Opinion on the Specific Application of Article 30 of the Customs Law" from the Legislative Affairs Commission of the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress

Fa Ban [2003] No. 236

To the High People's Courts of Liaoning, Tianjin, Shandong, Shanghai, Zhejiang, Hubei, Fujian, Guangdong, Hainan, and Guangxi, and all maritime courts:

We hereby forward to you the reply from the Legislative Affairs Commission of the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress regarding the specific application of Article 30 of the Customs Law, as requested by the General Administration of Customs. Please implement this in judicial work.

July 25, 2003

Legislative Affairs Commission of the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress

Reply Opinion on the Specific Application of Article 30 of the Customs Law

Fa Gong Wei Fu Zi (2003) No. 9

To the General Administration of Customs:

We have received your letter titled "Letter Requesting Study and Reply on the Specific Application of Article 30 of the Customs Law" (Shu Fa Han (2003) No. 74). After study, we hereby reply as follows:

1. In accordance with Paragraph 1 of Article 30 of the Customs Law, the party entitled to apply for the return of the surplus proceeds from the sale by Customs of imported goods that have not been declared within the prescribed time limit is the consignee of the imported goods.

2. The Customs Law does not define the term "consignee." This term shall be determined in accordance with common understanding and other applicable laws. According to common understanding and the relevant provisions of the Contract Law and the Maritime Code, "consignee" refers to the consignee named in the contract of carriage, or the consignee to order, or the holder of a bearer bill of lading, or any other person entitled to take delivery of the goods.

3. In accordance with Paragraph 1 of Article 30 of the Customs Law, where goods are sold by Customs as provided in this Article, if the goods are not subject to import restrictions, the consignee is entitled, within the prescribed time limit, to apply for the return of the surplus proceeds after the lawful deduction of relevant charges and taxes; the Customs shall return such surplus proceeds.

June 26, 2003
